name: Benign Partial Epilepsy of Infancy with Complex Partial Seizures
aliases: Infantile Partial Epilepsy with Complex Partial Seizures

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Benign Partial Epilepsy of Infancy with Complex Partial Seizures

criteria.description: Onset of seizures in infancy, typically between 3 and 24 months of age
Presence of complex partial seizures characterized by impaired consciousness and focal motor symptoms
Normal psychomotor development before and after seizure onset
Interictal EEG showing focal epileptiform discharges without generalized abnormalities
Spontaneous remission of seizures within a few years without neurological sequelae

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical age of onset, complex partial seizures, and normal development; EEG findings supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by EEG; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complex partial seizures with impaired consciousness
Focal motor seizures involving unilateral clonic movements
searchTerms: focal motor seizures on one side

pathognomonic.notes: Development remains normal despite seizure activity

common.symptomName: Automatisms such as lip-smacking or hand movements during seizures
Brief seizure duration typically less than 2 minutes
Seizure clustering over days or weeks

occasional.symptomName: Transient autonomic symptoms such as pallor or cyanosis during seizures
searchTerms: temporary pale or blue skin during seizures
brief autonomic changes like pallor or cyanosis

occasional.symptomName: Mild irritability or behavioral changes between seizures

searchTerms: abnormal brain activity in specific areas
seizures triggered by fever early on

rare.symptomName: Transient developmental delay during seizure clusters
searchTerms: temporary developmental slowdown during seizure clusters
transient delay in skills with seizure groups

imaging: Brain MRI usually normal or shows no structural abnormalities
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; genetic testing not routinely diagnostic
other: Interictal EEG shows focal epileptiform discharges, often temporal or centrotemporal

distinguishingFeatures: Seizures predominantly nocturnal with characteristic centrotemporal spikes on EEG
Typically older age of onset (3-13 years)
Simple partial seizures without impaired consciousness
No focal features or complex partial seizures

redFlags: Seizures refractory to standard antiepileptic treatment
references: Orphanet: Benign partial epilepsy of infancy with complex partial seizures (ORPHA:166299)
